A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LrcSSM research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, supporting reliable comparison across relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v3 reports original LrcSSM classification experiments on six datasets and ablations of state dependence and complex-valued parameters, alongside results attributed to prior work.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds PPG-DaLiA results, runtime and convergence measurements, additional recurrent-model comparisons, and new architectural ablations.

M1.justification: The core LrcSSM equations (8)–(14), architecture, and ELK procedure are retained. Appendix D extends the existing diagonalization approach to gated RNNs, giving a GRU construction and introducing MguSSM, GruSSM, and LstmSSM adaptations. Appendix E also constructs the constant-capacitance StcSSM variant.

E1.justification: All six original classification datasets remain. Appendix C adds PPG-DaLiA regression evaluation, extending task coverage to continuous-target prediction within physiological time-series modeling. This is a limited benchmark expansion with a distinct prediction requirement.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 add Transformer and RFormer comparisons, with scores attributed to the Rough Transformers paper. Table 9 introduces comparisons against MguSSM, GruSSM, and LstmSSM. The original nine baselines remain, while the evaluated comparator families expand substantially.

E3.justification: Table 6 changes the reported EigenWorms hidden dimension from 16 to 64; the PDFs do not establish whether this reflects rerunning or correcting the setting. Added experiments introduce PPG-DaLiA MSE evaluation, timing over 1,000 training steps, and fixed-architecture model comparisons. The original classification splits and tuning grid remain.

E4.justification: New Tables 10–11 directly test liquid versus constant capacitance and diagonal versus dense Jacobians, addressing central architectural choices previously untested in v3. Figure 2 adds convergence-iteration analysis. The earlier state-dependence and complex-parameter ablations remain as Tables 12–13.

E5.justification: v4 explicitly reports standard errors for aggregate accuracy in Table 3 and Tables 12–13, replacing v3's unlabeled aggregate uncertainty values. The latter captions also identify per-dataset standard deviations. Figure 2 adds iteration-distribution boxplots. The retained five-seed reporting does not indicate an increase in runs.

E6.justification: v4 adds regression, runtime, recurrent-model, and architectural-control results. Table 11 reports average accuracy of 65.4 for diagonal versus 63.3 for dense Jacobians. The new Transformer row changes the EthanolConcentration ranking: 40.5 versus LrcSSM's 36.9. Original classification accuracy values remain, including LrcSSM's 66.3 average, while its Table 3 uncertainty changes from 18.6 to 8.3 under standard-error reporting.

T1.justification: Appendix D.1 adds a gated-recurrence-to-ODE derivation, defines generalized diagonal A and b constructions, and works through the GRU case. These extend the mathematical formulation. The existing LrcSSM equations and Appendix A stability proofs and scaling arguments are unchanged.

C1.justification: v4 elevates preservation of performance under diagonalization and generalization to other nonlinear RNNs into abstract and contribution claims. It also adds Transformers to the abstract's empirical superiority claim. The explicit v3 contribution claiming priority in scaling a bio-inspired RNN is removed, substantially changing the contribution framing.

C2.justification: v4 adds explanations attributing diagonal-model performance to more efficient representations and interpreting the capacitance ablation as supporting nonlinear membrane capacitance. Appendix B.5 argues that convergence iterations impose little runtime overhead. The suggestion that adding a time feature could improve performance is removed; the existing Newton-iteration limitation remains.

D1.justification: v4 documents fixed dimensions and block counts for the additional recurrent-model comparisons, adds per-dataset timings with a 1,000-step basis, and revises the EigenWorms hidden-dimension entry. Table 6's new 'include time=False' column restates v3 Appendix B.4 rather than documenting newly changed preprocessing.

R1.justification: v4 adds references supporting GRU, LSTM, MGU, Rough Transformers, and PPG-DaLiA. The earlier references and main related-work discussion remain. Removing the explicit first-to-scale-bio-inspired-RNN claim modestly revises novelty positioning alongside the broader recurrent-model framing.

P1.justification: The abstract is rewritten, NSSM/LSSM terminology is revised throughout, and Sections 3.2–3.3 provide new signposting. Appendices are reorganized, with the former Appendix C ablations becoming Appendix E. Most existing methodological, background, discussion, and conclusion prose remains recognizable.

P2.justification: v4 adds five tables covering runtime, regression, recurrent-model comparisons, and two architectural controls, plus the convergence boxplot in Figure 2. Tables 1–3 gain comparator rows, and Table 6 gains a time-feature column. Earlier ablation tables are relocated and renumbered; the architecture diagram is retained.

improvement.justification: v4 addresses important empirical gaps in v3: Tables 10–11 directly test the capacitance and diagonalization choices, while Table 7 and Figure 2 provide concrete evidence about computational cost and convergence. These additions substantially strengthen scrutiny of the central design and efficiency arguments. Broader comparisons also expose limitations, although the retained claim of best EthanolConcentration performance now contradicts the added Transformer result, 40.5 versus 36.9. That inconsistency tempers, but does not outweigh, the stronger empirical foundation.
